title: Releasing Private Data for Numerical Queries

problem.claim: Many data-analysis tasks use numerical values that may be any real number.

gap.claim: Prior work on private data release studied only counting or linear queries with per-tuple contributions in [0,1].

contributions.claim: The paper presents a new mechanism to privatize a dataset D for a given set Q of numerical queries.
For each query w ∈ Q, the mechanism achieves error Õ (√n • Δw(D)), where Δw(D) is the maximum contribution of any tuple in D queried by w.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The instance- and query-specific error bound leads to excellent practical performance, according to the authors.

narrative_sequence.summary: Prior private data release work studied counting and linear queries with contributions in [0,1].
Many analytical tasks instead involve arbitrary real-valued data.
The paper introduces a mechanism for numerical queries with error Õ (√n • Δw(D)) per query.
The authors state that the instance- and query-specific bound also yields excellent practical performance.

source_observation.claim: The error bound depends on the maximum contribution of any tuple for each specific query.

interpretation.claim: Query- and instance-specific sensitivity can provide more targeted error guarantees than a single global bound.

application.claim: When designing private numerical-query mechanisms, consider bounds that adapt to both the dataset instance and the query.

exception.claim: The supplied abstract does not specify the assumptions or regimes under which this adaptation is advantageous.

unknowns: The abstract does not describe the mechanism’s construction or privacy parameters.
The abstract does not provide experimental setup, datasets, baselines, or numerical performance results.
